title: Honey and Coffee: How to Sweeten Your Cup Naturally
heading: Honey and Coffee: A Natural Way to Sweeten Your Cup
description: How to use honey instead of sugar or syrup in coffee — how much to add, hot vs iced, and why a chunky blend like SUBUR behaves differently.
keywords: honey instead of sugar in coffee
figureAlt: A spoonful of chunky, spiced honey drizzling into a mug of black coffee, with a jar of honey resting beside it on a wooden table

faqs.q: How much honey should I put in my coffee?
faqs.a: Start with one teaspoon for a standard cup and adjust from there — most people settle between one teaspoon and one tablespoon. Honey is sweeter than sugar by volume, so a direct swap usually needs less honey than the sugar it's replacing. Taste as you go, since preference varies.

faqs.q: Does honey dissolve in cold coffee or cold brew?
faqs.a: Not as easily as in hot coffee. Honey is thick, and cold liquid slows it down further, so stirred straight into iced coffee it can sink to the bottom instead of blending through. Dissolve it in a small splash of hot water first, then add that to the cold drink.

faqs.q: Why does SUBUR honey take longer to dissolve in coffee?
faqs.a: SUBUR is a thicker blend carrying raw honeycomb, nuts, and spices rather than clear, filtered honey. That texture means it needs a little more stirring to fully dissolve, and small flecks of nut or spice may settle at the bottom — which is normal for this kind of blend, not a flaw.

faqs.q: Can I add honey to a latte?
faqs.a: Yes — drizzle it over the foam instead of stirring it straight in, so the top is sweeter at first and the honey works through as you drink. A teaspoon is usually enough for a standard latte; add more only after tasting, since it's easy to oversweeten a milky drink.

faqs.q: Is honey a better choice than white sugar in coffee?
faqs.a: It's a different choice rather than a strictly better one. Honey is a natural sweetener with its own flavour, while white sugar is refined and neutral-tasting. It comes down to whether you want the coffee sweeter only, or to pick up some flavour from the sweetener too.

blocks.question: Can you put honey in coffee?
blocks.answer: Yes — honey works well as a natural sweetener in coffee, hot or iced. A teaspoon to a tablespoon stirred through black coffee, a latte, or cold brew replaces refined sugar with something that dissolves a little more slowly if it's a thicker blend like SUBUR, and adds its own flavour instead of pure sweetness. Start with less than you'd use in sugar and adjust to taste.

blocks.text: How Much Honey to Use in Coffee

For a standard 200-250ml cup, start with one teaspoon of honey and taste before adding more — most people land somewhere between one teaspoon and one tablespoon. Honey is sweeter than granulated sugar by volume, so a direct swap usually means using less than you think. Stir it in while the coffee is still hot enough to help it blend, or dissolve it first in a splash of hot water if you're making iced coffee.
Hot Coffee, Iced Coffee, and Cold Brew

Honey dissolves fastest in hot coffee, where the heat breaks it down almost as quickly as sugar. In iced coffee or cold brew, it behaves differently — cold liquid slows it right down, so honey stirred straight into a cold glass can sink and sit at the bottom instead of mixing through. The easier route for iced drinks is to stir the honey into a small amount of hot coffee or hot water first, then pour that over ice.
Why SUBUR Takes a Moment Longer to Dissolve

SUBUR isn't clear, filtered honey — it's a thicker blend built around raw honeycomb with star anise, saffron, fresh ginger, walnuts, nutmeg, cinnamon, black seed, and almonds folded through it. That texture means it takes a little longer to fully dissolve in a hot drink than a thin, filtered honey would, and you may notice small flecks of nut or spice settle at the bottom of the cup — that's the ingredients, not a flaw. Given the spice notes already in the blend, it tends to complement coffee's own flavour rather than just sweetening it.

blocks.text: Simple Ways to Add Honey to Your Coffee

items.text: Stir a teaspoon of honey straight into a hot black coffee — the honey's own spice notes come through once the coffee cools slightly.
Drizzle honey over the foam of a latte instead of stirring it in, so it sweetens the first few sips and settles through the rest.
Dissolve the honey in a splash of hot water first, then mix it into cold brew so it blends evenly instead of sinking.

blocks.text: If you haven't tried it, start with the simplest version: one teaspoon of SUBUR stirred into a hot black coffee, tasted before you add more. From there it's easy to adjust for a latte or cold brew. SUBUR honey is available through Berkat Madinah Store's Shopee and TikTok Shop pages, or in person at the Ampang Jaya and Batu Caves stores in Selangor.
